title: Shelf by Shelf - Part 6
body:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=H3JH96ZJWzM

Daniel (@dungeondive) returns to Shelf by Shelf after a long absence, working through two shelves of his library — and this instalment wanders further off the map than most.

The genre shelf is a vintage paperback haul: a likely first printing of Harry Harrison's Bill, the Galactic Hero, most of the Stainless Steel Rat series (recommended about as hard as Daniel recommends anything — Cowboy Bebop, forty years before Cowboy Bebop), the Deathworld trilogy, Samuel Delany's Dhalgren in several editions, Joe Haldeman's Mindbridge, Richard Paul Russo's underread Carlucci cyberpunk trilogy, and Vladimir Sorokin's genuinely strange Ice trilogy.

The detour that makes the video is Raymond C. Jones. Trawling Seattle's used bookshops, Daniel kept finding books stamped with that name and annotated in a cryptic private notation, and slowly realised he and this stranger had near-identical taste. He gathered twenty or thirty of them, entertaining the idea of reconstructing the man's library, then found the obituary: a few lines, noting only that he was an avid reader. Every lead since has dead-ended, and he asks on the off chance that anyone who knew him get in touch.

The second shelf is not genre at all. It is William Saroyan — the Fresno author whose museum room Daniel once maintained and whose daughter he has met — plus Steinbeck and Muriel Spark.

----

A shelf of secondhand books stamped by a stranger with your exact taste, and an obituary that says only that he was an avid reader. Whose library would you try to rebuild?
